question: The reaction in which a single reactant splits into the two or more simpler products is called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**decomposition reaction**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A **decomposition reaction** is a type of chemical reaction in which a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances.
 
• This reaction is generally endothermic, meaning it requires the input of energy in the form of heat, light, or electricity to occur.
 
• An example of a decomposition reaction is the breakdown of water (H₂O)
